analysis:
The batch contains only documentation changes, with no code, configuration or workflow changes. I found no concrete security regression.

1. docs/architecture/model-registry.md (head lines 17-22): a media-discovery guard says staged `nemotron_h_omni` checkpoints do not advertise media. The match is described as whitespace- and case-insensitive and independent of repo IDs or aliases. This narrows the advertised surface and is consistent with TB-007. The `ModelMediaPolicy.swift` implementation was not supplied, so the claim is unverified.

2. docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (head lines ~295-306): the plain unpublished Nemotron Super owner now joins the resident recurrent checkpoint bank. The bank is gated by `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY` opt-in and the global switch. The new `alignsRecurrentCheckpointsToPrefillChunks` rule captures checkpoints only at whole prefill-chunk multiples. Relevant threat: T-041, whose text says production has no RAM tier. That text appears to pre-date the opt-in resident banks described elsewhere in this doc. The new Nemotron Super eligibility does not change the opt-in gate or the `cacheSalt` tenant scoping. Later passes could check whether T-041 should mention opt-in resident tiers; this is a documentation gap, not a regression.

3. docs/architecture/inference.md: only head lines 1208+ were supplied. The patch excerpt for the new Nemotron Super local bridge (hunk at head lines 25-171) is truncated. That text says the bridge is unregistered with no HTTP route. It also says media, tools and client prompt-cache keys are rejected, and text prefix reuse runs only when the owner has a checkpoint bank. If the cache remains `cacheSalt`-scoped, this is consistent with T-041. The full hunk and the underlying Swift code (NemotronSuperLocal*) were not examined, which is a coverage limit.

No changes to endpoints, attestation, authorization or encryption were visible.
